title: 2022年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2022年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
passage:
P1 Even though we are living in an age where growing old is thought of as an inevitable misery, this doctor has been changing the game for seniors over the last 25 years.

P2 It all started in 1991 when the Harvard-educated physician was transferred from working in a stressful emergency room to being the medical director of a nursing home in upstate New York. The depressing and regimented(严格管制的) environment got him thinking on what exactly could improve the residents' conditions.

P3 Even though animals in nursing homes were illegal at the time, Dr. Bill Thomas took a chance. Based on a hunch(直觉), he brought in two dogs, four cats, hens, rabbits, 100 birds, a multitude of plants, a flower garden, and a vegetable patch.

P4 The change was dramatic. There was a 50% drop in medical prescriptions along with a dramatic decrease in death rates—but most importantly, the residents were simply happier.

P5 Dr. Thomas's approach, named the Eden Alternative, has driven nursing homes to allow a more autonomous(自主的) and creative living space for their elderly. It erases the belief that growing old means growing useless. He encourages residents to think of their age as an enriching new phase of life rather than the end of it.

P6 Thomas, now a speaker and author of several books, also created small, independently-run residences with their own bedrooms and bathrooms, and he has been preaching a singular message that getting old is not a bad thing.

P7 "Within six weeks, they had to send a truck around to pick up all the wheelchairs," Thomas told the Washington Post. "You know why most people in nursing homes use wheelchairs? Because the buildings are so big."

P8 The 56-year-old doctor's methods have been adopted in Australia, Japan, Canada, and America with enormous success. Last year he published Second Wind: Navigating the Passage to a Slower, Deeper, and More Connected Life, a guide on how to shift our perspectives on aging and growth.

P9 He is currently traveling through North America performing with his guitar and his enthusiasm on his Age of Disruption Tour.

questions.q: What has Bill Thomas been doing for a quarter of a century?
options: Transforming people's lifestyle.
Honoring his Harvard education.
Changing people's philosophy of life.
Shifting people's perspective on aging.
questions.explain:
【判型】What has Bill Thomas been doing for a quarter of a century? 用 what 直接问做了什 么事，且锁定了二十五年的具体时间，没有 infer/suggest/imply 等推断信号，也不问全文 主旨。

【拆句】现在完成进行时 has been doing 强调「一直在做、且仍在继续」，for a quarter of a century 是时间段状语；对应原文要找「持续二十五年都在做的那件事」。

【定位】Even though we are living in an age where growing old is thought of as an inevitable misery, this doctor has been changing the game for seniors over the last 25 years. 尽管我们生活在一个把变老视为难免之苦的时代，这位医生在过去 25 年里一直在为老年人 改变这一局面。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Transforming people\'s lifestyle 偷换了 changing the game 的对象——原文改变的 是观念/局面，不是 lifestyle（衣食住行的生活方式）。 B) 无中生有 Honoring his Harvard education 原文虽提 the Harvard-educated physician，但只 是介绍背景，并未说他二十五年所做的事是「为哈佛教育争光」。 C) 以偏概全 Changing people\'s philosophy of life 把「对变老的看法」扩大为「整套人生哲 学」，范围被无限放大，且对象从 seniors 变成了 people 全体。 D) ✓ 正确 growing old is thought of as an inevitable misery ↔perspectives on aging changing the game for seniors ↔Shifting people\'s perspective 预判说他在改变「对变老的看法」，Shifting people\'s perspective on aging 在字面 与语义上同时复现这一判断，无须额外推断。 为什么 Bill Thomas 要在养老院尝试一些不同的做法? A) 他想让养老院对老年人来说更加愉快。 B) 他想将自己在哈佛所受的训练应用于实践。 C) 他认为彻底改革养老院的管理是自己的责任。 D) 他对在这种环境中工作感到失望。

questions.q: Why did Bill Thomas try something different in the nursing home?
options: He wanted to make it more pleasant for seniors.
He wanted to apply his Harvard training to practice.
He felt it his duty to revolutionize its management.
He felt disappointed working in the environment.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why did Bill Thomas try something different in the nursing home? 用 why 直接问动 机，原文有明确的因果或心理描写句即可定位，不必跨段推断。 47. Why did Bill Thomas try something different in the nursing home? A) He wanted to make it more pleasant for seniors. B) He wanted to apply his Harvard training to practice. C) He felt it his duty to revolutionize its management. D) He felt disappointed working in the environment.

【拆句】一般过去时 did，问的是过去某次具体动机；try something different 是「尝试不一样的做 法」，对应原文「引入动植物」这一动作。

【定位】The depressing and regimented(严格管制的) environment got him thinking on what exactly could improve the residents' conditions. 那种压抑而管制严格的环境促使他思考究竟怎样才能改善住户的处境。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 improve the residents\' conditions ↔make it more pleasant for seniors 预判说「让老人住得更舒心」，make it more pleasant for seniors 在动宾结构与对象 层面同时复现，无需推断。 B) 无中生有 apply his Harvard training to practice 把 Harvard-educated physician 这一背景细 节拼到动机上——原文从未说他这么做是为了「把哈佛所学落地」。 C) 过度推断 felt it his duty to revolutionize its management 把「想改善老人处境」夸张成「觉得 自己有责任去革命化养老院管理」，原文既无「职责感」亦无「revolutionize management」的表述。 D) 张冠李戴 felt disappointed working in the environment 把 The depressing and regimented(严格管制的) environment 这一对环境的描写，错置成他个人情绪。原文 是环境压抑，而非他心情失望；且这是触发思考的背景，不等于动机本身。 关于 Bill Thomas 将动物和植物带入养老院,我们了解到什么? A) 他把养老院搞得一团糟。 B) 他做了所有专业人士都会做的事情。 C) 他赢得了州政府的即时支持。 D) 他的行为违反了州法律。

questions.q: What do we learn about Bill Thomas bringing animals and plants into the nursing home?
options: He made a mess of the nursing home.
He did something all professionals would do.
He won instant support from the state authorities.
He acted in violation of the state law.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about Bill Thomas bringing animals and plants into the nursing home? 锁定一个具体事件，问围绕它能从原文得到什么信息，无推断标记。

【拆句】动名词短语 bringing… into… 作介词 about 的宾语，整句问「关于他往养老院里搬动植物 这件事，我们能知道什么」。

【定位】Even though animals in nursing homes were illegal at the time, Dr. Bill Thomas took a chance. 尽管当时养老院里养动物是违法的，比尔·托马斯医生还是冒了险（这么做了）。 48. What do we learn about Bill Thomas bringing animals and plants into the nursing home? A) He made a mess of the nursing home. B) He did something all professionals would do. C) He won instant support from the state authorities. D) He acted in violation of the state law.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 made a mess of the nursing home 把引入动植物说成「把养老院弄得乱七八糟」，与 原文完全相反——原文紧接着是 dramatic decrease in death rates 和 the residents were simply happier，效果是正面的。 B) 与原文相反 did something all professionals would do 说这是「所有专业人士都会做的事」，但 原文 Dr. Bill Thomas took a chance 与 animals in nursing homes were illegal at the time 都指向「冒险特例」，并非行业常规。 C) 与原文相反 won instant support from the state authorities 把 took a chance（冒险）反向虚构 成「立即获得州政府支持」，与原文「违法」事实完全冲突。 D) ✓ 正确 animals in nursing homes were illegal at the time ↔acted in violation of the state law 预判抓住「违法」这一事实，acted in violation of the state law 用名词 violation＋介 宾 of the state law 复现了 illegal，语义重心一致。 Bill Thomas 一直坚持倡导什么? A) 健康并非只是年轻人的特权。 B) 养老院的规模应受到严格限制。 C) 变老绝不是什么悲惨的事情。 D) 老年人住所应该独立运营。

questions.q: What has Bill Thomas been persistently advocating?
options: Good health is not just a privilege of the young.
Nursing homes should be strictly limited in size.
Getting old is by no means something miserable.
Residences for seniors should be run independently.
questions.explain:
【判型】What has Bill Thomas been persistently advocating? 问的是他一贯主张的具体内容；原 文有「preaching a singular message」句可直接对接，仍属细节题。

【拆句】现在完成进行时 has been advocating＋副词 persistently 强调持续性；what 是 advocating 的宾语前置。

【定位】Thomas, now a speaker and author of several books, also created small, independently-run residences with their own bedrooms and bathrooms, and he has been preaching a singular message that getting old is not a bad thing. 如今他既是演讲者又是几本书的作者，他建立了独立运营、带独立卧室和卫生间的小型住 所，并一直在传播一个核心讯息：变老并不是一件坏事。 49. What has Bill Thomas been persistently advocating? A) Good health is not just a privilege of the young. B) Nursing homes should be strictly limited in size. C) Getting old is by no means something miserable. D) Residences for seniors should be run independently.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Good health is not just a privilege of the young 把话题从「对变老的看法」偷换成 「健康权」；原文虽提 50\% drop in medical prescriptions，但讨论的是养老院环境 改善的效果，并未上升为「健康是不是年轻人专属」的命题。 B) 以偏概全 Nursing homes should be strictly limited in size 借用 the buildings are so big 这 一例证，伪装成他的「长期主张」。原文只是用大养老院解释轮椅多，并未上升为「养 老院必须严格限制规模」的口号。 C) ✓ 正确 getting old is not a bad thing ↔Getting old is by no means something miserable think of their age as an enriching new phase of life rather than the end of it ↔ Getting old is by no means something miserable 预判核心是「变老不糟糕」，Getting old is by no means something miserable 在主 谓宾与否定逻辑上完全复现这一判断。 D) 以偏概全 Residences for seniors should be run independently 借用 created small, independently-run residences 这一具体做法，伪装成他的中心主张；但 preach a singular message 后的同位语清楚说明他反复在传的核心讯息是 getting old is not a bad thing，而非「独立运营」。 Bill Thomas 的新理念受到了怎样的反响? A) 它正在许多国家获得认同。 B) 它正在世界范围内引发热烈讨论。 C) 它在各地都被认为具有革命性。 D) 它正在赢得政府的认可。

questions.q: How is Bill Thomas's new concept received?
options: It is gaining ground in many countries.
It is being heatedly debated worldwide.
It is considered revolutionary everywhere.
It is winning approval from the government.
questions.explain:
【判型】How is Bill Thomas\'s new concept received? 问「被如何接受」，原文必有一句直陈反 响的句子，无须跨段推断。

【拆句】一般现在时被动语态 is received，主语是 new concept，问外界对其评价；how 在句首作 方式状语。

【定位】The 56-year-old doctor's methods have been adopted in Australia, Japan, Canada, and America with enormous success. 这位 56 岁的医生的方法已经在澳大利亚、日本、加拿大和美国得到采纳，并大获成功。 50. How is Bill Thomas's new concept received? A) It is gaining ground in many countries. B) It is being heatedly debated worldwide. C) It is considered revolutionary everywhere. D) It is winning approval from the government.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 have been adopted in Australia, Japan, Canada, and America ↔ gaining ground in many countries with enormous success ↔gaining ground 预判强调「被多国接受、正在扩展」，gaining ground in many countries 同时复现 「多国」与「势头良好」两个要点。 B) 与原文相反 being heatedly debated worldwide 把「被接受」反扭成「被激烈争论」，原文 enormous success 是正向评价，没有任何争议、反对的语义。 C) 以偏概全 considered revolutionary everywhere 既无原文支持的「革命性」评价，又把多国采 用扩大为「everywhere」——原文只列了四国，不能等同于「到处」。 D) 无中生有 winning approval from the government 凭空虚构「获得政府批准」，原文只说被采 用并成功，未指明任何一个政府机构层面的官方批准。
